markdown_report:
The next experiment should complete the exported-predictor audit before changing BERT4Rec training. At 30% progress, this addresses a documented uncertainty with bounded computation and no additional fitting. The audit tests deployment consistency; improved recommendation quality remains a separate hypothesis.

**Insights from the supplied evidence**

1. All four categories pass four live fixtures with zero reported score discrepancy. Exported checkpoint, mapping, routing and host-device consistency remain unresolved.
2. Movies user 8675 has training-recovery catalog rank 425 yet expected sampled HR@10 of 0.999856. Candidate-set effects explain this coexistence without establishing a defect or generalization gain.
3. Margin probes inspected zero batches. Missing provenance and deployment observations identify integration gaps rather than failed supervision.

**Insights from related work**

1. [Metamorphic testing](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) motivates predictable transformations. Candidate permutation and valid batch partitioning complement differential comparisons but cannot certify correctness.
2. [PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html) supports frozen snapshots and explicit reloads. Hash agreement establishes identity relative to a manifest, while behavioral assertions test computation.
3. [Numerical-accuracy guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) requires aligned device, precision and execution settings. [Unstable tied top-k indices](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html) require separate score and selection checks.

Three directions follow: establish deployment identity, calibrate behavioral checks, then investigate history dependence.

| Layer | Question | Present gap |
|---|---|---|
| Consumed training | Were targets and loss constructed correctly? | Missing captures |
| Exported inference | Does deployment implement the selected checkpoint? | Unverified parity |
| Recommendation quality | Does ranking generalize? | Requires pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas remain feasible. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Artifact identity gate — 3/7/3.** Originality: useful integration, established hashing. Potential: catches stale exports, cannot certify computation. Difficulty: compact manifest, actual-load instrumentation required.
- **Fault-calibrated export replay — 4/7/7; selected.** Originality: integrates family-specific boundaries, established testing methods. Potential: localizes faults, gives no direct preference gain. Difficulty: no retraining, substantial independent reconstruction and CUDA-path instrumentation.
- **Position-preserving history substitutions — 5/7/5.** Originality: combines frequency and positional controls, familiar perturbations. Potential: motivates masking experiments, measures dependence rather than intent. Difficulty: scoring reuse, demanding availability/semantic matching.

Freeze artifacts, construct inputs independently and invoke the actual exported predictor in a fresh process on the host CUDA path. Compare identities, tokens, features where observable, finite scores and native selections. Use an additional canonical score/ID total order before every chunk truncation; preserve evaluator tie behavior and distinguish policy differences from faults. Validate with hand-calculated fixtures, verified mutations and harmless controls; reserve fixtures and mutation families before calibration. Report numerical boundary effects, unsupported instrumentation and partial completion explicitly. Bounded tests can overfit their fixtures and share reference errors; passing results do not certify deployment generally. Retain exactly one trained BERT4Rec checkpoint/category and unchanged host macro validation HR@10 for selection.

idea.description: Implement a bounded, fault-calibrated differential audit of the actual exported working/predict.py against a reference loaded from the same selected BERT4Rec checkpoint, augmented with independently calculated fixtures and justified metamorphic relations. Separately assess artifact identity, category routing, canonical input construction, observable features, candidate scores, native ranking and simulator full-catalog selection on the actual host CUDA path. Reference reloads execute identical trained parameters solely for auditing; they are never additional fitted predictors or sources of fused recommendations.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish agreement on bounded live fixtures but leave fresh-process export parity unverified. Training-recovery examples demonstrate that sampled and catalog outcomes can differ predictably, while embedding alignment and qualitative feedback do not identify a deployment defect. An aligned-device audit addresses the unresolved implementation boundary; independent fixtures, explicit tie policies and held-out fault checks reduce shared-reference errors and audit overfitting. No validation improvement or immediate-choice inference is claimed.
idea.implementation_notes:
This remains an integration specification, not executable replacement training code: the supplied workflow summary does not include the actual baseline sampler, predictor API or writer implementation. Preserve the report's three directions. Complete the bounded deployment audit first; pursue position-preserving history substitutions as a subsequent separate single-model experiment, particularly if the audit finds no actionable defect. Avoid expanding the audit indefinitely at the expense of the shared search budget.

After existing checkpoint selection, freeze a trial-local manifest containing category, checkpoint-byte hash, architecture configuration, reserved padding and MASK IDs, sequence length, preprocessing seed, training seed, canonical ordered item-map hash, catalog-ID fingerprint and exported source hash. Record checkpoint-selection step and effective scoring configuration. Create immutable snapshots rather than mutable references to a live state_dict. Hashes establish identity relative to this manifest, not independent authenticity or correctness. Instrument actual artifact loading to report resolved paths, hashes and the loaded route; echoing expected values does not certify loading. Verify Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl independently. Production must load exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint per category.

Construct reference inputs through a separate implementation grounded in explicit history events and mapping contracts, without calling the exported preprocessing helper. Retain history[-(L-1):], append the reserved MASK, then left-pad to L. Read the greatest nonpadding absolute position, L-1 for this construction, never nonpadding-count minus one. Use empty, singleton, short, unequal-padding, repeated-item, exactly L-1-history and overlength fixtures. For training-history audit cases, use only supplied public training events. Earlier repeated IDs remain legitimate historical events. Verify real-ID mapping round trips, reserved-token exclusion and category-specific catalog bounds. Do not expose a shifted target through bidirectional input or change the corrected masked-target training policy.

Predeclare eight fixture cases/category: empty, singleton, short, unequal-padding batch, repeated-item, exact retained-window boundary, overlength truncation and a catalog-ID boundary case. Reserve the exact-window and ID-boundary cases for final checks before examining calibration results. Add small, independently calculated selection fixtures with explicit scores and IDs covering ties at the cutoff, irregular final chunks, exclusions and fewer than k eligible items. These fixtures test indexing and selection independently of a learned network. They do not establish full-network correctness. Record every fixture, expected property and partition in the audit artifact.

Invoke the actual exported public prediction interface in a fresh process; do not replace it with a diagnostic implementation. Keep its candidate order, return semantics and scorer. Where supported, instrument the actual internal path to expose consumed token IDs, candidate IDs, readout index, selected features and loaded artifact identities. Compare exact IDs and indices before numerical comparisons. If tracing or feature access is unavailable, retain black-box comparisons and report internal construction/readout as unverified. Preserve the public predictor interface and update the embedded predictor writer whenever inference code changes.

The primary comparison must run sequential reference and exported executions on the actual single host CUDA device with aligned software versions, model weights, dtype, autocast, TF32 settings, attention backend, batch shape, sequence length, candidate layout and scoring chunk policy. Record Python, PyTorch, CUDA and device versions plus effective precision/backend settings. Use evaluation/inference mode. If the architecture uses functional scaled_dot_product_attention, explicitly supply dropout_p=0.0 for evaluation; model.eval() alone does not override that argument. Do not silently change production kernels or precision to make comparisons pass. Controlled backend or deterministic reruns may diagnose discrepancies, but must be labeled separately from the native production configuration. CPU reload is an optional secondary check and cannot establish CUDA parity. Sequential reloads must not exceed single-GPU memory; no simultaneous reference ensemble is needed.

Require finite scores before filtering. For aligned FP32 comparisons, predeclare atol=1e-5 and rtol=1.3e-6, applying abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). These are initial explicit criteria, not universally justified constants. If native execution uses another dtype or materially different kernels, predeclare a justified criterion before inspecting discrepancies or report the comparison as unresolved; do not tune tolerances retrospectively. Report maximum absolute error, maximum relative error using denominator max(abs(reference), 1e-8), elementwise pass counts, nonfinite counts and observation counts. Report feature errors separately from score errors. Numerical closeness does not imply ranking agreement.

Maintain two explicitly separated selection comparisons. Native parity uses the actual production/simulator filtering and tie semantics, preserving the pinned host evaluator unchanged. A separate diagnostic canonical selection uses descending computed score followed by ascending canonical mapped item ID, with exact equality defining ties. Apply that total order before every chunk-local and merged truncation; sorting only an already selected top-k cannot repair tied-cutoff membership. If native ties are unspecified or differ, report the difference as a policy issue or tie ambiguity, not automatically an implementation failure. A later production tie-policy change requires an explicit predictor-writer update; the audit itself does not silently enact one.

Retain explicit item IDs through catalog scoring, filtering, chunk merging and selection; candidate enumeration indices are not item identities. Stream scores over the fixed real-item catalog, excluding padding and MASK and applying the native full-history unseen-item policy for the twenty designated real training users, five/category. Do not infer ownership from repetition. For a diagnostic target-restored training-recovery case, retain its separately declared eligibility policy; never substitute that policy for native unseen-item recommendations. Record catalog/mapping fingerprints, history/exclusion fingerprints, eligible counts, score computation and returned IDs. Compare uniqueness, eligibility, reserved-token exclusion, top-10 set overlap, ordered equality and target-rank agreement only where a legitimate target exists. Do not manufacture targets or HR metrics for simulator recommendations.

Use the production chunk size as the primary reference computation. On bounded small fixtures and at most one designated user/category, also compare chunk sizes 1024 and 4096 where supported, forward/reversed catalog traversal, candidate permutation with score realignment, repeated execution, singleton versus batched inference and valid batch splitting. Preserve sequence order. Candidate-specific scores should realign under permutation only when the predictor specification guarantees independent candidate scoring; otherwise report the relation unsupported. Shape and traversal changes can legitimately change floating-point scores. Record numerical discrepancies separately from exact rank/selection differences and investigate boundary cases rather than asserting universal cross-shape invariance.

For a shared finite eligible universe, let epsilon be the maximum absolute score difference over all its items and let gap be the reference kth-minus-(k+1)th score. If gap > 2*epsilon, top-k membership is protected under the compared score arrays. Report this as a derived numerical diagnostic, not a universal guarantee: it requires complete score coverage, identical filtering and item alignment, and does not establish internal order within the selected set. With fewer than k+1 eligible items, the boundary gap is undefined. Small gaps or exact ties can explain membership changes without establishing a defect; large-margin discrepancies warrant investigation. If complete epsilon is unavailable, do not certify stability from sampled errors.

Predeclare a 60-second timeout per fresh-process invocation and a 300-second aggregate audit wall-time cap per category, including subprocess startup and secondary comparisons. Reserve within that cap time for the five native-user catalog checks; log uncompleted work explicitly rather than extending the cap after seeing results. Record synchronized GPU-active duration where measurable, total wall time, subprocess count, completed fixtures/users/chunks and failures so the host can charge execution against the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Terminate timed-out child processes and release their device resources. Partial coverage remains incomplete, never a pass. CPU work is also logged and subject to host accounting.

Inject faults only into disposable trial-local copies and run sequentially. Retain five operators: wrong-category routing, incorrect checkpoint identity, one-sided item-map permutation, omitted appended MASK and count-minus-one readout on short left-padded histories. An incorrect-checkpoint artifact must be a clearly recorded altered copy of this category's current artifact, never another trial's checkpoint. A metadata-only or behavior-preserving alteration tests identity alone; changing tensor values must be verified separately if behavioral sensitivity is claimed. Wrong routing that fails catalog compatibility may test rejection rather than numerical sensitivity. Independently verify each operator's intended property, changed values and applicability before invoking the detector.

Separate calibration from final detector evaluation. Use routing, checkpoint identity and omitted-mask operators for calibration on the six calibration fixtures; reserve one-sided map permutation and count-minus-one readout as final operator families with independently predefined applicability fixtures. Freeze assertions and thresholds before running these reserved operators and the two held-out fixture cases. If debugging requires inspecting or modifying the reserved suite, record that adaptation and downgrade claims of independent final evaluation; do not silently reuse it as untouched evidence. The small fixed suite does not support broad statistical claims about unseen fault families.

For each operator report attempted, inapplicable, invalid injection, verified corruption, proven-equivalent, unresolved, detected, surviving, expected rejection, unexpected crash and timeout counts. Distinguish identity-gate failures, explicit input/artifact rejections and behavioral score/rank kills. Do not count an invalid injection, infrastructure crash or timeout as successful behavioral detection. Where a verified incompatible artifact is explicitly rejected by the intended guard, report this as rejection detection separately. Survival on sampled fixtures does not establish equivalence. Define each detection rate with its own verified, applicable, non-equivalent denominator; zero denominators are null. These bounded rates do not estimate real-world fault prevalence.

Keep harmless controls: unchanged fresh reload, consistent batch-row permutation, valid batch splitting and candidate permutation followed by inverse alignment. Retain consistent relabeling as an optional control only where all ID-dependent structures, input histories, item maps, embedding rows, output rows, biases and exclusions can be transformed correctly while preserving reserved tokens. Under canonical ID-based ties, relabeling need not preserve tied ordering after mapping back; use tie-free fixtures or explicitly test the corresponding transformed order. Independently verify control preconditions and record unsupported controls. Restoration must reproduce original artifact hashes and inputs. Report false alarms over verified harmless controls separately from numerical boundary discrepancies.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) and every supplied ModelView interface. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data remain compatible. Add optional explicit export-runner and frozen-manifest transport without changing diagnostic tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B×L. Missing runner, manifest, provenance or tracing produces null with a reason. Do not infer deployed parity from live ModelView scores. Retain family-safe integrity, embedding, margin and consumed-record probes; use predict_score rather than assuming embedding dot products if the scoring architecture changes.

Do not advance the production loader or create hidden extra training iterations. Run bounded diagnostics from explicit captures or public histories, preserving their exposure labels. Restore every module's prior mode, main-process Python/NumPy/Torch CPU/CUDA RNG states and modified precision/backend controls in finally. Worker-local RNG, loader progress and exact training restart remain outside this guarantee. Aggregate audit coverage across categories only after collecting all four results; a single-category ModelView must not fabricate a four-category macro.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve the twenty designated native simulator users and pinned host validation with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Do not access hidden test files, alter splits, fetch extra data/pretrained weights or change the evaluator. No additional fitted scorers, independently trained experts, checkpoint averaging or score fusion are introduced. Only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects model revisions.

The audit adds no learned component, but the underlying network can retain memorization, exposure/popularity shortcuts and broad-relevance biases despite passing every check. Repeatedly adjusting detectors to the same fixtures creates audit overfitting; adaptive validation queries can also overfit the fixed cohort. Log detector revisions, diagnostic queries, validation queries and budget use. Shared preprocessing or scoring mistakes can survive differential agreement, which is why hand-calculated cases and justified metamorphic relations remain necessary. Ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item-category metadata and simulator traits remain unavailable. Titles, descriptions and histories do not establish immediate purchase intent, ownership or compatibility without explicit evidence. Passing this bounded audit demonstrates only the reported deployment consistency and detector sensitivity, not complete correctness, convergence, user usefulness or held-out gains.
idea.pseudocode:
after_existing_checkpoint_selection():
    manifest = freeze_trial_local_selected_artifacts_maps_catalog_config_and_writer()
    suite = predeclare_fixtures_fault_partitions_controls_tolerances_and_caps()
    attach_optional_transport(manifest, actual_export_runner, suite)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = save_module_modes_main_process_rng_precision_and_backends()
        try:
            result = existing_bounded_family_safe_diagnostics_without_production_iteration()
            if export_transport_missing():
                return add_null_with_reason(result, 'export_audit')
            # This invocation may expose only one category; aggregate externally.
            category = current_explicit_category()
            budget = start_predeclared_category_cap(seconds=300)
            canonical = independently_construct_fixture_tokens_and_ids(
                left_padding=True, append_reserved_mask=True,
                readout='greatest nonpadding absolute position')
            verify_hand_calculated_mapping_filtering_and_tied_selection_fixtures()
            reference = sequential_reference_reload_on_host_cuda(
                manifest, canonical, native_execution_settings=True)
            actual = fresh_process_call_actual_export(
                category, suite.public_inputs, timeout_seconds=60)
            compare_actual_loaded_artifacts_and_route(actual, manifest)
            compare_exact_traced_ids_readout_and_features_when_available(actual, reference)
            compare_finite_scores_with_predeclared_tolerances(actual, reference)
            compare_native_rankings_without_changing_native_tie_rules()
            compare_separate_canonical_selection(
                total_order='descending score, ascending canonical item ID',
                apply_before_every_truncation=True)
            run_verified_harmless_controls_and_bounded_shape_chunk_checks(budget)
            for operator in suite.calibration_operators:
                mutant, evidence = inject_into_disposable_current_trial_copy(operator)
                status = independently_verify_applicability_and_changed_property(evidence)
                record_gate_rejection_behavioral_detection_or_unresolved(status, mutant)
            freeze_detector_version_and_thresholds()
            run_reserved_fixtures_and_operator_families_once_with_adaptation_log(budget)
            for user in designated_native_training_users(category):
                if budget.exhausted():
                    record_incomplete_user(user)
                    continue
                ref_catalog = stream_all_native_eligible_ids_and_scores_with_explicit_ids(user)
                actual_selection = call_actual_native_catalog_selection(user)
                compare_native_ids_exclusions_counts_and_order(ref_catalog, actual_selection)
                compare_canonical_total_order_selection_separately(ref_catalog)
                if_complete_aligned_score_arrays_compute_epsilon_gap_and_membership_bound()
            return add_metrics_definitions_operator_counts_cost_and_unavailable_reasons(result)
        finally:
            terminate_any_remaining_audit_children()
            restore_module_modes_main_process_rng_precision_and_backends(state)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_using_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish=['artifact identity', 'native CUDA parity', 'CPU secondary evidence',
                     'canonical selection policy', 'numerical boundary effects',
                     'unverified internals', 'calibration versus reserved checks',
                     'training recovery', 'host validation'],
        require=['denominators', 'fault verification', 'control preconditions',
                 'partial completion', 'query/adaptation log', 'cost', 'unavailable reasons'],
        prohibit=['invented gains', 'equivalence inferred from survival',
                  'causal intent claims', 'ensemble proposals'])

originality.positive: Integrates actual CUDA export execution, explicit item identity, native versus canonical selection, independent fixtures and reserved fault families within the fixed BERT4Rec contract.
originality.negative: Differential, metamorphic and mutation testing are established; the proposal contributes a careful task-specific protocol rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can localize deployment faults and provide a reusable gate before controlled single-model learning experiments.
future_potential.negative: Its value depends on finding actionable discrepancies; bounded audit success provides no direct validation gain and cannot resolve the reported immediate-choice failures.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional fitting or backbone change, and explicit caps constrain diagnostic execution.
code_difficulty.negative: Actual-path CUDA instrumentation, independent mapping and selection logic, reproducible subprocesses, chunk-boundary handling and verified reserved faults require substantial integration.

related_work.title: 2024 empirical study of metamorphic testing for recommender systems
contributions: The supplied search summary reports six metamorphic relations evaluated across LibRec, PREA and Surprise.
Motivates predictable transformations when complete output oracles are unavailable.
limitations: Does not independently validate the proposed BERT4Rec deployment mutations.
Each harmless transformation requires explicit preconditions for the actual predictor.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents checkpoint reload and evaluation-mode practices.
Explains the mutable best-state reference pitfall relevant to selected-checkpoint snapshots.
limitations: Does not certify item mappings, category routing, artifact authenticity or exported recommendation behavior.

related_work.title: RecTools transformer tutorial
contributions: Provides a documented precedent for BERT4Rec appended-mask inference.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of this host's predictor writer or left-padding readout.

related_work.title: PyTorch ONNX export verification documentation
contributions: Provides a precedent for numerical comparison between reference and exported execution.
limitations: Numerical agreement alone does not establish ranking agreement near ties.
The Python predictor audit does not require or assume ONNX conversion.

related_work.title: TensorFlow Recommenders Streaming retrieval documentation
contributions: Documents explicit candidate identifiers and exclusions in streaming retrieval.
Highlights the distinction between supplied item identifiers and candidate enumeration indices.
limitations: Its API contract does not certify the PyTorch implementation.
Canonical tied-cutoff membership requires an explicitly implemented total order.

related_work.title: TensorFlow Recommenders factorized top-k implementation
contributions: Illustrates streaming chunk-local retrieval and merging.
limitations: An illustrative implementation does not guarantee this audit's ID mapping or tie policy.
A moving repository branch is not an immutable reproduction artifact; record the consulted revision if implementation details are adopted.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains device, batching, reduction-order and precision differences.
Supports aligned native-CUDA comparisons and explicit reporting of TF32 and dtype settings.
limitations: Does not supply a universal tolerance for this BERT4Rec model.
Cross-device discrepancies alone do not establish a deployment defect.

related_work.title: PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention documentation
contributions: Documents backend-dependent execution and explicit dropout_p behavior.
Supports checking evaluation dropout and recording effective attention backends.
limitations: Applies directly only if the implementation uses this functional operator.
A controlled backend comparison does not replace testing native production settings.

related_work.title: PyTorch topk documentation
contributions: Documents that indices for tied elements are not guaranteed stable.
Motivates explicit total ordering before diagnostic truncation.
limitations: Does not prescribe the pinned evaluator's tie policy.
Sorting a selected subset cannot repair incorrect membership at a tied cutoff.

related_work.title: PyTorch testing documentation
contributions: Defines explicit absolute and relative numerical-comparison criteria.
limitations: Passing score tolerances does not imply exact ranks or top-k membership agree.

related_work.title: PyTorch deterministic algorithms documentation
contributions: Provides controls useful for repeatability and diagnostic reruns.
limitations: Does not guarantee cross-device or cross-version equality.
Changing determinism settings can alter native execution and must be reported separately.

related_work.title: Herbold and Tunkel: differential testing across machine-learning frameworks
contributions: The supplied search summary describes legitimate implementation differences that complicate differential bug signals.
Motivates aligned semantics and independent expected cases.
limitations: Does not validate this specific checkpoint-export audit.
Agreement between pseudo-oracles can preserve shared errors.

related_work.title: Panichella and Liem: mutation testing for machine learning
contributions: Questions assumptions transferred from conventional mutation testing to learned systems.
Motivates explicit operator validity and restrained interpretation of mutation scores.
limitations: Does not establish realism or coverage of the five proposed deployment operators.

related_work.title: Study of equivalent mutants
contributions: Provides methodological context for distinguishing equivalence from undetected mutations.
limitations: Survival on a bounded fixture set cannot establish behavioral equivalence.
Operator-family holdouts here are a proposed evaluation design, not a guarantee from the source.

related_work.title: Saha and Kanewala: metamorphic testing and mutation detection
contributions: The supplied search summary reports limited mutant detection for previously proposed classifier relations.
Motivates complementary checks and empirical measurement of detector sensitivity.
limitations: Classifier results do not quantify recommender or BERT4Rec fault coverage.
Sensitivity depends on selected relations, inputs and fault populations.
